objective: Make a failed local Minecraft connection release its adapter session so the owner can correct the server or LAN port and reconnect without restarting Desktop.
non_goals: Do not start, scan for, or expose a Minecraft server automatically.
Do not add automatic retry, public targets, pathfinding, combat, mining, model authority, or persistence.
Do not change the owner-only loopback control boundary, session-secret handling, or emergency-stop latch.
contracts: A pre-spawn error, kick, end, timeout, or factory failure leaves no resident bot or listener and exposes a bounded lastError.
After a non-emergency failed connection, the controller status is disconnected and an owner may start exactly one new connection attempt.
Stale callbacks from a released bot cannot alter a newer attempt.
The Desktop clearly distinguishes the Minecraft main menu from a listening server and explains that an Open-to-LAN world uses its displayed port, while 25565 is the usual dedicated-server default.
allowed_dependencies: Existing workspace dependencies only; no new dependency.
acceptance_criteria: A simulated ECONNREFUSED error rejects as E_MINECRAFT_CONNECT, releases the first bot, preserves the bounded error, and permits a second injected bot to connect.
An old bot event after retry cannot disconnect or corrupt the current bot session.
The owner gets actionable LAN/server-port guidance without any automatic network discovery or retry.
Minecraft adapter tests, Desktop production tests, module-brief validation, GitNexus diff impact analysis, and git diff check pass.
required_test_commands: uv run --frozen python -c "import json; from jsonschema import Draft202012Validator; schema=json.load(open('docs/schemas/module-brief.schema.json', encoding='utf-8')); brief=json.load(open('docs/modules/M09-S6B-connect-retry-hotfix-module-brief.json', encoding='utf-8')); Draft202012Validator(schema).validate(brief)"
